# Cache Valley Appliance Repair — Safe Launch SOP

Current truth: Matt has formed the LLC, but formal appliance-repair training, tooling and operating systems are still being built. Kevin must never describe Matt as certified, licensed, trained or equipped beyond verified reality.

## Launch sequence
1. Verify Idaho/local business, tax, insurance and any occupation-specific requirements from authoritative sources.
2. Define a narrow starter service scope that matches Matt's proven competence.
3. Build the minimum safe diagnostic/tool kit.
4. Complete training and practice on representative appliances before accepting that job family.
5. Establish intake, model/serial capture, diagnostic evidence, estimate approval, parts sourcing and post-repair verification.
6. Establish pricing that covers drive time, diagnosis, labor, parts risk, callbacks, overhead and taxes.
7. Launch only when blocking readiness gates are satisfied.

## Safety boundary
Kevin may research, organize, calculate, draft forms and recommend training/tools. Kevin may not invent credentials, bypass electrical/gas safety, authorize customer work, purchase equipment or represent Matt to customers without owner approval.
